points.description: States that a linked list is passed to a function by reference (i.e., via a reference or pointer to the head node, so the function works on the original list rather than a copy), using the term 'by reference'.
points.partial_credit: Half: says the list is passed via a pointer to the head/head node but does not use the term 'by reference' or does not say it is the original list.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes this from pass by value: the list/head is not copied, so changes made inside the function (e.g., to the head or nodes) affect the original list.
points.partial_credit: Half: mentions only that changes persist or that no copy is made, without contrasting with pass by value.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise statement 'by reference' (reference/pointer to the head) plus the contrast with pass by value. Answers saying only 'by pointer' or vaguely 'using the head' earn at most part marks on P1. Saying 'by value' or any wrong statement about the passing method earns nothing on that point.
